Below is a generalized, professional-level workflow for editing and enhancing images using advanced image-editing software (e.g., Adobe Photoshop, Affinity Photo, or GIMP). The emphasis is on non-destructive techniques, precise control, and industry-standard best practices.

1. Workspace Preparation  
   1.1. Calibrate your monitor and set up a consistent color environment (use a hardware calibrator).  
   1.2. Create a well-organized folder structure: RAW/, Exports/, PSDs/, Assets/.  
   1.3. In Photoshop: set Color Settings to Adobe RGB (1998) or a profile matching your output medium; in Affinity, ensure Document Color Format and ICC profiles are correct.

2. Import & Raw Conversion  
   2.1. Open RAW in Adobe Camera Raw (ACR) or Lightroom.  
   2.2. Correct white balance using eyedroppers and custom temperature/tint.  
   2.3. Apply lens-profile corrections (distortion, vignetting).  
   2.4. Adjust basic sliders: Exposure, Contrast, Highlights/Shadows, Whites/Blacks.  
   2.5. Enable “Auto” for a starting point, then fine-tune manually.  
   2.6. Output to a 16-bit TIFF or Smart Object to preserve data.

3. Composition & Crop  
   3.1. Use the Rule of Thirds, Golden Ratio, or custom guides.  
   3.2. Straighten horizons with the Ruler tool.  
   3.3. Crop to final aspect ratio, leaving room for bleed (print) or safe area (web).

4. Non-Destructive Base Adjustments  
   4.1. Create Adjustment Layers (Levels, Curves, Exposure).  
       – Levels: set black/white points.  
       – Curves: craft an S-curve for contrast; isolate channels for color balancing.  
   4.2. Use Masks to localize adjustments (paint on the mask with a soft brush).  
   4.3. Smart Objects: convert layers to Smart Objects before applying filters or transforms.  
   4.4. Organize layers in groups (e.g., “Tone & Contrast,” “Color Grading,” “Retouch”).

5. Advanced Color Grading  
   5.1. Use Selective Color or Hue/Saturation Adjustment Layers to tweak individual channels.  
   5.2. Employ Color Lookup Tables (LUTs) for cinematic looks—fine-tune Opacity.  
   5.3. Create Gradient Maps for split toning (shadows and highlights).  
   5.4. For precision, switch to Lab color mode: modify the ‘a’ and ‘b’ channels to remove color casts.

6. Detailed Retouching & Texture Enhancement  
   6.1. Frequency Separation for skin or texture:  
       – High frequency layer: details.  
       – Low frequency layer: color/tones.  
       – Retouch seamlessly with Clone Stamp or Healing Brush on each frequency.  
   6.2. Dodge & Burn on 50% gray, Overlay-mode layers:  
       – Dodge (lighten) to bring out highlights.  
       – Burn (darken) to deepen shadows and sculpt form.  
   6.3. Remove unwanted elements:  
       – Content-Aware Fill for large areas.  
       – Spot Healing for small blemishes.  
       – Pen Tool + Layer Mask for precise object removal.

7. Compositing & Creative Modifications  
   7.1. Extract subjects with Select and Mask (refine hair edges with Decontaminate Colors).  
   7.2. Place subjects into new backgrounds—match perspective and lighting with Transform > Warp or Perspective Warp.  
   7.3. Use Blend If sliders (Layer > Blending Options) to seamlessly blend layers by luminosity.

8. Sharpening & Noise Management  
   8.1. Apply noise reduction first (e.g., Camera Raw’s Noise panel or specialized plugins).  
   8.2. High Pass sharpening on a merged Smart Object:  
       – Duplicate the flattened, converted Smart Object.  
       – Apply Filter > Other > High Pass (radius ~1–3px).  
       – Set blending mode to Overlay or Soft Light; mask as needed.  
   8.3. For web, apply Unsharp Mask at 0.3–0.5 pixels, 50–80% amount; for print, increase radius slightly.

9. Creative Effects & Finishing Touches  
   9.1. Subtle vignettes with a Curves or Gradient fill layer masked to edges.  
   9.2. Light leaks or lens flares: add as Smart Objects, set blending to Screen/Lighten, adjust opacity.  
   9.3. Use layer comps (Photoshop) to save multiple looks or color grades.  
   9.4. Check your image in both 8-bit and 16-bit to ensure no banding.

10. Soft Proofing & Output  
   10.1. Soft-proof for print: View > Proof Setup > Custom, selecting the printer profile.  
   10.2. Tweak any colors that fall outside the print gamut with Gamut Warning.  
   10.3. Export settings:  
        – For web: Export As… JPEG/PNG with sRGB, “Convert to sRGB” checked.  
        – For print: Save as TIFF, 300 dpi, include printer profile, no compression or LZW if transparency needed.  
   10.4. Generate versions: high-res master, web-optimized, social-media crops, and thumbnail.

11. Automation & Quality Control  
   11.1. Record Actions or use Scripts to batch-process repetitive tasks (watermarks, resizing, metadata).  
   11.2. Inspect at 100% magnification; look for artifacts, halos, or banding.  
   11.3. Archive your PSD/AFPHOTO/GIMP file with all layers intact for future revisions.

By adhering to a structured, non-destructive workflow and leveraging these advanced techniques—frequency separation, smart objects, precise color grading, and layer-based compositing—you’ll achieve professional-level results in any image-editing project.
